title: Compassion of Christ
definition: The compassion of Christ is His merciful and active care toward the weak, suffering, sinful, burdened, and lost.
summary: Jesus sees the needy and moves toward them with mercy, truth, and help.
christFocus: Christ reveals the compassion of God by healing, teaching, welcoming, forgiving, and laying down His life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus' compassion is not distant pity. He sees real need and moves toward people with mercy and truth. He cares for the sick, grieving, hungry, demon-oppressed, ashamed, and lost.

His compassion is holy. He does not excuse sin, but He moves toward sinners to save and restore them.

The cross is the deepest display of His compassion, where He bears sin for those who could not save themselves.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people believe Christ is annoyed by weakness or ashamed of their brokenness. The compassion of Christ matters because He welcomes the weary and gives mercy.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring weakness and need to Jesus. Then reflect His compassion by moving toward sufferers with truth, mercy, and practical care.
